newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's IRI studies offers for Stet unit.
newsitem.headline: Italy's IRI studies offers for Stet unit.

text.p: Italian state industrial holding IRI said on Wednesday it had received 26 valid offers for the publishing arm of telecom holding Stet, which it would now study.

IRI said 20 of the offers for publishing division Seat had come from foreign companies and six from Italian firms. The Italian government has demanded that Seat be sold off before Stet's privatisation, which is slated for the Spring of 1997.
Analysts believe Seat could be worth more than $2.0 billion.
Stet, controlled by IRI, said on Wednesday it was calling an extraordinary shareholders' meeting for October 30 to get approval for the planned demerger of Seat.
Iri did not say when it would decide who would get Seat, nor did it name any bidder.
However it said 11 of the offers came from companies operating in the telecommunications and publishing sector, of which two were Italian and the rest foreign.
A total 15 bids had come from financial institutions and investment funds, of which four were Italian and 11 foreign.
IRI added that two of the 26 bids had come from a consortium of companies, but gave no further details.
Lehman Brothers, which is handling the Seat sale for IRI has been contacted by interested companies from Europe, Asia, Australia and the United States.
Newspapers said last month that U.S. telephone company GTE was planning to make an aggressive bid for a 61 percent stake in Seat. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
